exăcerbātĭo , ōnis, f. exacerbo,
I.an exasperation, Rufin. de Schem. 11, p. 274: peccatorum, i. e. because of, Salv. Gub. Dei, 4, 7.—
II. Esp., of the stirring of divine anger by the Jews in the wilderness, the provocation, Vulg. Hebr. 3, 8; 15.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
